statement_en: Let $1<q<1+\epsilon$ and consider the set of numbers of the shape $\sum_{i\in S}q^i$ (for all finite $S$), ordered by size as $0=x_1<x_2<\cdots$. Is it true that, provided $\epsilon>0$ is sufficiently small, $x_{k+1}-x_k \to 0$?
statement_lean:
open Filter
open scoped Topology

theorem erdos_21558 :
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ q, 1 < q → q < 1 + ε →
    ∀ x : ℕ → ℝ, StrictMono x → Set.range x = { ∑ i ∈ S, q ^ i | S : Finset ℕ } →
    Tendsto (fun k => x (k + 1) - x k) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry
